page.layout: One printed page: title block centred at top (heading lines), then a poem of italic verse with a large woodcut initial at left; below it a centred dedication line and signature name. No margin notes.

main_text.head: EPOS
In Opus elegans
VIRI Clarissimi,
D. M. GERARDI de VRIES, Philosophiæ in Academia Patria Doctoris & Professoris Ordinarii.
main_text.p: Ǖmine naturæ naturam Numinis optas Nosse via facili plenè solidèque? Revolve, Quæ tibi conceditFRISIUS,Meletemata; multum, Quod juvat, invenies. Nam quævis linea spirat Ingenium subtile Viri Mentemque subtilem: Seu monstret verum, damnosave falsa refutet Dogmata, quæ Veteres docuere, Novique Sophistæ Fortiter incukant ac ore manuque tuentur. Sæpius adspicies (reliquas si vertere Chartas Expetis) ingenuæ Libertatisque decoræ Signa. Probat reprobatque nihil, quod Nomina tantum Æstimet. Hoc servum deceat pecus! Unica flectunt Hunc Ratio, Divina Fides. His subdere Fasces Judicii Sapientis erit, quem cana loquetur Posteritas, quem Fama vehet super Ætheris Orbes.
Ita lusit Collegæ Philosopho, Philosophus Collega

page.notes: The large initial "I" is a decorated woodcut letter; read as "Ǖmine" in the opening line, likely "Vmine" (Immine). The word "subtilem" in the line "Mentemque subtilem" is doubtful and may read "subjectam" [?]. Some letters in the signature block are faded. Faint show-through and stains at the lower left and right are not transcribed.
